input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Argument.get_help_record returns self.help unchanged, so the second element of the tuple is None for an undocumented argument even though format_arguments now feeds every record straight into formatter.write_dl without a fallback.
- failure path: A command declares two arguments and sets help on only one; running it with --help makes write_dl measure and wrap a None description and the help command crashes with a TypeError instead of printing usage.

Reviewer finding
- description: Argument.get_help_record now returns (metavar, self.help) without converting a None help to an empty string, so an undocumented argument produces a None description in the row list.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with one argument that has help text and another positional argument with no help. format_help_text's guard passes because any arg has help, so write_dl receives a row whose second element is None. The formatter's width measurement calls term_len on every cell, and term_len on None raises TypeError. Impact: `--help` crashes for any command that mixes documented and undocumented positional arguments, which is a common case.
critique: The finding points to the same faulty operation: get_help_record returns self.help unconverted, so a None description goes into write_dl. It describes the same way it fails: mixing documented and undocumented arguments makes term_len raise a TypeError during --help. Its mention of format_help_text instead of format_arguments is a minor naming difference and does not change the mechanism.
